title: One-off error-mode inventory (overnight scratch)
content:
Context:
- Quick overnight pass on a weird error mode seen in nightly smoke for dedicated cluster (eu-west-1). Low volume but high-severity when it occurs: factual contradictions + spuriously long answers. Not consistent across prompts.

Summary of observed regression:
- Time window: 2026-03-09 02:00–04:30 UTC (approx).
- Symptoms: occasional hallucination bursts where model asserts incorrect facts with high confidence; also observed long-winded replies that repeat the same point several times (verbosity loop).
- Surface changes around period: small runtime kernel bump (runtime-kernel v3.14.1 -> v3.15.0) deployed to a canary pool 2026-03-08; quantization config tweak for int8 fallback on some older GPUs; tokenization micro-optimizations landed in repo (PR #7162) 2026-03-07.

Quick ad-hoc rubric (for spot checks) - 1..5 (5 = best):
- Correctness: 1..5 -> note common hallucination behaviors
- Hallucination severity: 1..5 (5 = none)
- Verbosity control: 1..5 (5 = concise)
- Repetition/loop probability: 1..5 (5 = none)
- Token efficiency (extraneous tokens): 1..5
- Latency/timeout: 1..5 (5 = within SLO)

Spot samples I pulled (short prompts + two representative outputs):
- Prompt A: "Summarize the latest EU data-protection changes affecting cloud vendors."
  - Baseline (expected): "The recent EU updates focus on data transfer safeguards, clearer vendor obligations for processing, and tighter breach notification timelines (GDPR-aligned updates; see EDPB guidance, 2025)."
  - Nightly (regressed): "The EU enacted a new law in 2026 called the Cloud Safety Act which requires on-premises data mirroring and fines up to 10% of global revenue. Vendors must store all logs for 7 years."
  - Rubric scores: Correctness=2, Hallucination=1, Verbosity=4, Repetition=5, Token efficiency=2, Latency=5
  - Notes: invented law name, wrong fine numbers, wrong retention period. High-confidence assertion language.

- Prompt B: "Give a short checklist for integrating Redwood Dedicated into a CI/CD pipeline."
  - Baseline (expected): "1) Obtain API key; 2) Add deploy step to CI; 3) Configure model pinning and rollout; 4) Add smoke tests and cost alerts; 5) Monitor token-level metrics."
  - Nightly (regressed): "1) Sign up for Redwood Dedicated; 2) Stand up VPC; 3) Mirror all data to on-prem; 4) Run weekly manual audits and keep an audit spreadsheet; 5) Configure model pinning (optional). Also some small motivational text here repeating step 3."
  - Rubric scores: Correctness=3, Hallucination=2, Verbosity=2, Repetition=2, Token efficiency=2, Latency=5
  - Notes: suggests unnecessary/incorrect mandatory steps for typical Dedicated integration; adds repetition and filler.

Hypotheses (short):
1) Tokenization micro-optimizations changed segmentation for certain EU-specific tokens, unexpectedly altering model input distribution and prompting hallucination (rare but plausible).
2) Quantization-int8 fallback path has edge-case behavior that modifies softmax temperatures or logits ordering for low-probability tokens, increasing confident hallucinations.
3) Kernel change introduced a race where KV-cache fetch sometimes returns stale vectors for first few tokens in a request, causing the model to drift into parroting incorrect statements and loops.
4) Noisy prompt preprocessing in canary path: whitespace trimming bug caused concatenated sentence boundaries in a subset of requests.

Immediate checks to run (manual):
- Re-run the two prompts on latest stable runtime (v3.14.1) vs canary (v3.15.0) with identical env and same model variant. Record logits/topk for first 32 tokens.
- Force model to return token-level probs in debug mode and diff the distributions.
- Run tokenizer.compare on the same inputs and diff token counts/IDs.
- Re-run with quantization disabled to see if hallucination frequency drops.
- Check S3 logs for requests during window to see if special header variants correlated with failures (e.g., X-Trace or custom flags).

Quick commands / places to run checks:
- Local quick-curl: curl -X POST https://canary-api.redwood.internal/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' -d '{"prompt":"...","debug_tokens":true}'
- Eval harness: repo: infra/evals/nightly-smoke -> run `python run_smoke.py --samples 100 --variant canary`
- Tokenizer tool: repo: infra/token-tools -> `python -m token_tools.compare "input.txt" --show-ids`

Notes + heuristics observed while spot-checking:
- Hallucinations tend to assert specific numeric claims (years, fines, retention periods) rather than generic falsehoods. Hypothesis: model prefers numeric hallucinations when confused by tokenization or low-prob tokens.
- Repetition loops often start after the model uses an odd connective token sequence; loop begins at 2nd sentence.
- When I disabled quantization locally, at least one sample reverted to expected output (encouraging).
- Not all prompts affected — high-coverage prompt patterns (policy/legal, regulatory) seem more brittle.

Tickets / ops next steps (todo):
- Make a minimal reproducer with deterministic seeds and attach to JIRA-ENG-2345 (me).
- Add telemetry to canary to export token-probability diffs for a small sample window.
- Roll back runtime kernel in the canary pool if reproducer is confirmed.
- Run full nightly smoke with quantization disabled to compare failure rate.
- Share short notes + 3 examples with Solutions Eng + Legal for awareness (they may have seen customer reports).

Questions / open investigations:
- Is there any A/B config around tokenizer flags in canary? (ask infra/tokenizers team)
- Which exact commit in PR #7162 changed token merging heuristics? Need to bisect.
- Do we have per-device quantization stats broken out by GPU driver version?

Notes to self (freeform):
- Keep samples short; avoid too many moving parts (no function-calling tests right now).
- If logs show repeated identical token probabilities across requests -> suspect KV or cache reuse bug.
- Consolidate into a Confluence page once reproducer is stable. For now, keep this as a messy scratchpad.

Quick timeline suggestion for MWF sync:
- Mon: gather deterministic reproducer + add to ticket.
- Wed: run canary vs stable comparison, link plots.
- Fri: decide rollback or escalate to release-eng.

End of scratch. Will refine once I have deterministic reproducer and token-diff outputs.
